## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kuntinījātaka* (Ja 343) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. According to its traditional introductory account, the Buddha delivered the story while residing at Jetavana concerning a heron that dwelled in the house of the king of Kosala, opening with the verse line "Long I held" [SuttaCentral]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*) preserved in the commentary edited by V. Fausböll, the female bird (*sakuṇikā*) explains that she can no longer reside there, takes leave of the king, and flies away to the Himalayas [Fausböll 1883]. The Master then resolves the birth story by identifying that the heron of that time was the heron of the present, while the Bodhisatta was the king of Bārāṇasī [Fausböll 1883]. Variant manuscript readings documented in Fausböll's edition attest to spelling variations between *kuntanī* and *kuntinī* [Fausböll 1883].
No curated parallels in other Buddhist traditions or canonical collections are registered by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. Automated text analysis by DharmaNexus identified no internal Pali text reuse, but records weak machine alignments between verses of the text and the Tibetan *Bhoṭasvāmidāsagurulekha* (D4194) [DharmaNexus].
